newsitem.title: TAIWAN: ADB eyes Dec 6 for T$7bln Taiwan-dollar bond issue.
newsitem.headline: ADB eyes Dec 6 for T$7bln Taiwan-dollar bond issue.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank has set December 6 as the tentative date for its T$7 billion (US$255 million) Taiwan dollar-denominated bond issue, lead underwriter Chinatrust Bank said on Tuesday.
"The date is still awaiting final confirmation, which we expect to come soon," Chinatrust spokeswoman Wang Li told Reuters.
The issue would probably have a term of seven or 10 years, the spokeswoman said.

The December issue would be the second issue by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) denominated in Taiwan dollars and reflects a drive by Taiwan's government to encourage international agencies to raise capital in the island's cash-flush money market.

Taiwan's central bank, which approved the issue earlier in November, has said the ADB's bond issues would help internationalise the island's bond market and raise the credibility of Taiwan's currency.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million.
